headline: The bounce changed hands: a violent squeeze in metals, Brazil and China, while AI leadership, bitcoin and the long bond all refused to confirm.
summary: Risk regime slipped to -21 from -19 even as every index closed green, because the composition of the rally got worse, not better. The money went into the most beaten-up hard assets on the board: silver +9.5% to 43.85 (still 5th percentile of the year, 34% below its 200-day), platinum +5.2%, gold +3.5% to 3661, copper +4.8% to 5.5875 (1m z=-2.45). Miners levered it — GDXJ +4.5%, GDX +4.3% and +12.7% on the week, NEM +3.9%, FCX +3.2%, COPX +3.0%, XME +2.6% — and gold/silver collapsed 5.4%. The second leg was EM short-covering: EWZ +10.6% as USDBRL fell 4.4% to 5.5653 (-6.2% on the week), Shanghai +3.7%, KWEB +4.7%, FXI +2.3%, Hang Seng +2.1%, EEM +2.1% with EEM/SPY +1.5% and acceleration z=0.65 off a 10th-percentile base. Yesterday's momentum winner went the other way: Sensex -1.2%, INDA -1.1% and USDINR +0.8% after a 1m z of 3.23. This is the lowest-quality 15% of the tape being repriced, not a new bull impulse.

What did not confirm is the list that matters. On a +0.7% S&P day, NVDA fell 1.9%, GOOGL -0.8%, AMD -1.1% and SMH managed only +0.7% versus XME's +2.6%; SMH/SPY still carries a 1m z of -3.11 and MTUM -3.20. Bitcoin went the wrong way outright — BTC -2.2% to 59,189 at the 1.6th percentile of the year, ETH -2.6%, IBIT -1.7% — the single most liquidity-sensitive asset declining into a global squeeze. VIX closed up 0.2% at 26.85 on an up day, and while VIX3M fell 2.5%, the term structure at 1.0476 is still inverted with a 1m z of 2.12. The long end also leaned against it: TLT -0.7% with 30s at 5.30% and the 10-year real yield at 2.79%, acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day.

The plumbing is unchanged from Tuesday's prints and that is the problem — HY OAS 3.72 (+34bp on the month, 97th percentile), IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 both at the 100th percentile of the year, CCC 14.05 (+520bp YTD). HYG/IEF rose 0.3% today but sits at a 1m z of -1.61 and is rolling over; the credit & vol composite is -61. The front end still prices a hike: 3-month bills 4.36% against 3.88% effective funds, SOFR 3.95%, 2s10s 0.24 (-4bp, 7th percentile), 3m10y 0.51 and -27bp on the month. Against that, 5y breakevens are 2.13% (z=-1.62) and 10y 2.12% at the 0th percentile while core CPI accelerates (z=0.93, turning up) and core PCE runs 3.26% — a market pricing a policy mistake at both ends simultaneously. The dollar kept grinding into the squeeze: DXY +0.2% to 103.92 at the 95th percentile, EURUSD 1.0945 at the 3rd, USDCHF +0.6%, USDMXN at the 100th percentile.

Where the real economy shows through, the split is sharp. The consumer's cost base is bifurcating: gasoline -22.5% and WTI -18.3% on the month, but natural gas +7.6% today to 3.518, +24.9% on the month with acceleration z=1.14 and 18% above its 200-day, landing on UMich sentiment of 48. Labor remains fine — claims 189k at the 0th percentile, continuing claims -5.3% on the week. The domestic equity bid is still defensive-cyclical and non-AI: HD +13.7%, COST +14.8%, TGT +16.4%, WMT +11.2%, MCD +12.7% on the month, RSP/SPY at a 1m z of 3.27 and the 99.8th percentile. But the housing leg that led last week stalled today — ITB -0.2%, DHI -0.8%, XHB/SPY -0.6% with the 30-year mortgage back at 7.21% and permits -7.2%. Trade the dispersion; do not pay up for the index.

good.text: Deep-value hard assets caught a genuine squeeze: silver +9.5%, platinum +5.2%, copper +4.8%, gold +3.5%, with miners levering it (GDX +4.3% and +12.7% on the week, GDXJ +4.5%, COPX +3.0%). GDX/gold is turning up with 1m z=0.42 after gold miners spent three months -22.6%.

EM funding stress eased hard where it was worst: USDBRL -4.4% to 5.5653 (-6.2% on the week) with EWZ +10.6%, while USDCNY at 6.6441 sits at the 0th percentile of the year and China risk inflected — Shanghai +3.7%, KWEB +4.7%, FXI +2.3%, HSI +2.1%, EEM/SPY +1.5% with acceleration z=0.65.

The median stock keeps working: SPW +0.6% today and +4.7% on the week, RSP/SPY at a 1m z of 3.27 and the 99.8th percentile, IWM/SPY +0.3%, Russell 2000 +5.7% on the week. Breadth is broadening underneath a cap-weighted index that is still -6.6% on the month.

Energy disinflation is real at the pump: gasoline -22.5% and WTI -18.3% on the month, Brent -3.7% today to 91.14, DBC 1m z=-2.57. That plus 5y breakevens at 2.13% (z=-1.62) is the main argument that the hike being priced into 4.36% bills is the last one.

Back-end volatility is bleeding out: MOVE -2.3% to 95.3 and -10.4% on the week, VIX3M -2.5%, VIXTS down 2.6% from 1.0761 to 1.0476. Labor data stays benign — initial claims 189k at the 0th percentile, continuing claims -5.3% on the week.

bad.text: Credit has not participated in any of this. HY OAS 3.72 (+34bp on the month, 1m z=1.14), IG 0.98 and BBB 1.22 both pinned at the 100th percentile of the year, CCC 14.05 at +520bp YTD. HYG/IEF carries a 1m z of -1.61 and is rolling over; the credit & vol composite is -61.

Bitcoin fell on a global risk-on day — BTC -2.2% to 59,189 at the 1.6th percentile, ETH -2.6%, IBIT -1.7%, MSTR -44.8% on the month. The most liquidity-sensitive asset in the digest is still making lows while everything else squeezes.

AI leadership stalled: NVDA -1.9%, GOOGL -0.8%, AMD -1.1%, ASML -0.4% while the index rose. SMH is -25.0% on the month and 19% below its 200-day, SMH/SPY 1m z=-3.11, MTUM z=-3.20, ORCL at the 2nd percentile of the year. The bounce is being led by what was cheapest, not by what leads.

The front end still prices tightening and the curve keeps flattening into it: 3m bills 4.36% versus 3.88% funds, SOFR 3.95%, 2s10s 0.24 at the 7th percentile (-4bp), 3m10y 0.51 (-27bp on the month). The 10-year real yield at 2.79% has acceleration z=0.69 and TLT fell 0.7% today with 30s at 5.30%.

Spot vol refuses to break: VIX +0.2% to 26.85 on an up day, 1m z=2.28, term structure still inverted at 1.0476 (z=2.12) after the S&P's +4.6% week. St. Louis Fed stress is turning up (+0.80 on the week) and bank reserves are -1.4% on the month.

The dollar is still grinding higher through the squeeze — DXY +0.2% to 103.92 at the 95th percentile, EURUSD at the 3rd, USDCHF +0.6%, USDMXN at the 100th percentile — and the housing trade stalled: ITB -0.2%, DHI -0.8%, XHB/SPY -0.6% with mortgages back to 7.21% and permits -7.2%. Natural gas +24.9% on the month is a fresh tax on a 48 sentiment print.

trades.name: Gold miners over the metal
trades.line: Long GDX vs short GLD: miners finally leading bullion
trades.expr: Long GDX, short an equal dollar of GLD. Add GDXJ for a third of the long leg if you want more torque.
trades.thesis: Gold is -9.6% on the month and 17.5% below its 200-day, but miners have stopped underperforming: GDX/GOLD is turning up with a 1m z of 0.42 and +9.3% on the week. Operating leverage off a washed-out base, with no view required on the bullion direction that a 2.79% real yield still threatens.
trades.trigger: GDX +4.3% versus GLD +1.6% today, GDX +12.7% and GDXJ +12.7% on the week, NEM +3.9%, while gold/silver fell 5.4% — the classic signature of a precious complex bottoming through the equities first.
trades.stop: GDX/GLD giving back the week's 9.3% ratio move, or GDX closing back below the prior week's low while gold is flat.
trades.target: Another 10-12% of ratio gain, taking GDX/GOLD back toward its 3-month highs.

trades.name: Fade the crypto non-confirmation
trades.line: Short MSTR and IBIT: crypto fell on a global risk-on day
trades.expr: Short MSTR as the high-beta leg, half-size short IBIT alongside. Use puts if you want defined risk into a thin holiday tape.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin at 59,189 is at the 1.6th percentile of its 52-week range, -27.2% on the month and 17.6% below its 200-day, and it declined while silver squeezed 9.5% and EWZ gained 10.6%. When the most liquidity-sensitive asset cannot rally in a liquidity squeeze, the marginal buyer is gone. MSTR, -44.8% on the month, is the levered expression.
trades.trigger: BTC -2.2%, ETH -2.6%, IBIT -1.7% today against SPX +0.7%, RUT +0.9% and EEM +2.1%; the whole complex bounced only 1-3% on a week when the S&P added 4.6%.
trades.stop: BTC reclaiming its 200-day area (roughly 18% above spot) or MSTR rallying through the prior month's breakdown level on expanding volume.
trades.target: BTC retesting the lows with MSTR down another 18-20%.

trades.name: Software over silicon
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH into the semi bounce
trades.expr: Long IGV, short an equal dollar of SMH. Sell the semi leg into strength rather than chasing the pair.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being refunded, not refueled. IGV/SMH is +14.2% on the month and +13.7% in three, turning up, while SMH is -25.0% on the month, -19.0% below its 200-day and SMH/SPY carries a 1m z of -3.11. Software has the cashflow; semis have the capex bill and the inventory.
trades.trigger: SMH bounced 6.4% on the week but could only manage +0.7% today while NVDA fell 1.9%, AMD -1.1% and ASML -0.4%; MU is still -37.5% on the month. The bounce gives you a better short entry, not a trend change.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH reversing more than 7%, or NVDA reclaiming its 200-day — that would mean the capex cycle re-rates higher.
trades.target: Another 10% of relative outperformance; IGV/SMH back toward the levels it held before the AI blow-off.

trades.name: Bear flattener, own the belly not the tail
trades.line: Long IEF vs short TLT: 30s at 5.30% keep bleeding
trades.expr: Long IEF, short 1.0x dollar TLT (roughly duration-overweight the long leg). Cash bonds or the ETF pair both work.
trades.thesis: The curve is flattening from the wrong end. 3m10y is 0.51 and -27bp on the month, 2s10s at 0.24 is the 7th percentile, and the front end prices another hike with bills at 4.36% versus 3.88% funds. Meanwhile breakevens at 2.12-2.13% say the long end is absorbing term premium, not inflation: the 10y real yield is 2.79% with acceleration z=0.69 and 22% above its 200-day.
trades.trigger: TLT -0.7% today against IEF -0.2% while equities rallied — the long bond would not join a risk bounce, with 30s at 5.30% and mortgages back at 7.21%.
trades.stop: 3m10y re-steepening above 0.75, or 30-year yields breaking below 5.10% — that is the market pricing cuts again and the pair stops working.
trades.target: 5% on the combined position, consistent with 30-40bp of further 10s30s cheapening.

trades.name: China internet off a 0th-percentile yuan
trades.line: Long KWEB: CNY strongest in a year, Shanghai +3.7%
trades.expr: Long KWEB, with a half-weight FXI sleeve for the large-cap index beta. Scale in on down days; keep it a 3-5% book position.
trades.thesis: USDCNY at 6.6441 is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -6.1% year-on-year — the PBoC is tolerating a strong currency, which historically precedes a domestic risk bid. KWEB at -34.9% YTD and the 8.5th percentile is the most discounted large liquid equity exposure in the digest, and acceleration has turned positive (acc z=+0.2) even with the trend still down.
trades.trigger: KWEB +4.7%, Shanghai +3.7%, FXI +2.3% and Hang Seng +2.1% today; China relative strength versus the S&P is +3.2% to +5.7% on the month against a -10% three-month base.
trades.stop: USDCNY back above 6.75 or KWEB closing below the recent low — a renminbi devaluation impulse kills the trade.
trades.target: KWEB back to its 200-day, roughly 17% higher.

trades.name: Natural gas divergence
trades.line: Long nat gas: +24.9% on the month as crude collapses
trades.expr: Long front natural gas futures (or UNG equivalent), sized small — this is the highest-variance idea on the sheet.
trades.thesis: Gas is the only energy market in an uptrend: +24.9% on the month, 18.5% above its 200-day, trend turning up with acceleration z=1.14, while WTI is -18.3% and gasoline -22.5%. At the 20th percentile of its 52-week range it is cheap relative to its own history, and winter demand plus LNG pull is a different driver than crude's supply glut.
trades.trigger: +7.6% today to 3.518, +3.1% on the week, on a day Brent fell 3.7% to 91.14 — the divergence inside the energy complex is widening, not closing.
trades.stop: A close back below 3.10 (roughly the 1-month breakout level) or the 200-day giving way.
